 Economic Indicators EIA is raising its 2027 gasoline and diesel price forecasts as supply stays tight
 The agency projects 2027 diesel at $5.03 a gallon, up 12% from last month's forecast, and gasoline at $3.73, up 5%
 By Cris Tolomia · 2 min read · Updated November 10, 2026 Add QZ to Google Bloomberg / Getty Images
 The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) raised its forecasts for 2027 retail gasoline and diesel prices on Tuesday, citing continued supply constraints in global petroleum product markets.
 In its November Short-Term Energy Outlook, the agency projects U.S. retail diesel will average $5.03 a gallon in 2027, 12% above the $4.49 it forecast last month. It sees gasoline averaging $3.73 a gallon, 5% above last month's $3.56 forecast. Both prices are still projected to fall from 2026, when the agency expects diesel to average $5.25 a gallon and gasoline $3.89.
 The EIA said it assumes global petroleum product markets will face supply constraints through the end of 2027. Those conditions will support wider crack spreads, which measure refiners' margins, and encourage elevated U.S. refinery operations, the agency said.
 The EIA expects the Brent crude oil spot price to stay near $100 a barrel for the rest of 2026. It forecasts Brent will fall gradually to an average of $77 a barrel in the fourth quarter of 2027 as depleted global inventories build. The forecast assumes most Middle East production outside Iran returns to pre-conflict averages by the middle of 2027.
 Crude prices rose for a third consecutive month in October, the agency said, as falling global inventories, attacks on oil tankers in the Persian Gulf, constrained shipping capacity and higher transportation costs tightened supply. U.S. commercial crude oil inventories fell to 410 million barrels at the end of October, the lowest end-of-October level since 2014.
 The EIA also expects worldwide use of liquid fuels to shrink by 2 million barrels daily in 2026, with the shortfall made up in 2027, according to Bloomberg .
 The agency finalized its model inputs on Nov. 5, and the forecast does not specifically account for market events after that day.
 The outlook follows an October warning from the International Energy Agency that global diesel markets will remain under strain well into 2027 . The IEA said then that depleted inventories were unlikely to be replenished before the second half of next year.
 On Oct. 15, the IEA's Governing Board agreed to accelerate the release of its remaining oil stocks , including more than 20 million barrels of diesel, citing continued tightness in oil markets.
